title: Your Gin & Tonic Is Only As Good As Your Tonic
subtitle: And most people don’t think about it at all.
summary:
A gin and tonic looks simple, which is probably why it gets overlooked. Most people focus on the gin and barely think about the tonic.

But tonic isn’t neutral. It’s bitter, slightly sweet, and it makes up most of the drink. If it’s off, the whole thing feels flat, no matter how good your gin is.

sections.title: Tonic Is Doing Most of the Work
sections.body:
In a gin and tonic, tonic water is the majority of the drink. That means it’s carrying most of the flavor, the carbonation, and the overall structure.

If it’s too sweet, too flat, or just dull, there’s nothing the gin can do to fix it.

sections.title: Not All Tonics Taste the Same
sections.body:
Some tonics are crisp and citrusy. Others are heavier, sweeter, or more bitter.

That means the same gin can taste completely different depending on what you pair it with.

sections.title: Why Most Gin & Tonics Taste Flat
sections.body:
Flat usually means one of two things: the tonic is too sweet, or it’s lost its carbonation.

Either way, the drink loses that clean, refreshing edge and just feels heavy.

sections.title: Match the Tonic to the Gin
sections.body:
Lighter, citrus-forward gins pair better with clean, crisp tonics. More herbal or bold gins can handle something slightly more bitter.

It doesn’t have to be complicated — just intentional.

sections.title: What to Pay Attention To
sections.body:
If your gin and tonic feels dull or overly sweet, the tonic is usually the problem.

Try a different one and you’ll notice the difference immediately.
